subject: maths
question: When an article is sold at 5 percent discount, then there is a profit of 14 percent. If the discount is 11 percent, then what will be the profit ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of MP to CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%)

MP ÷ CP = (100 + 14) ÷ (100 − 5) = 114 ÷ 95 = 6 ÷ 5

Let CP = 500 and MP = 600. New Discount = 11% of 600 = 66.

New SP = 600 − 66 = 534. Profit = 534 − 500 = 34.

Profit% = (34 ÷ 500) × 100 = 6.8%.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.8 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Discount (D₁) = 5%

Initial Profit (P₁) = 14%

New Discount (D₂) = 11%

**Formula Used:**

MP ÷ CP = (100 + P%) ÷ (100 − D%)

SP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f0910474ebe8aacad944d7ab5d586a5b080eaf20a0bc5cf889fe9533da813a10.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ MP ÷ CP = (100 + 14) ÷ (100 − 5)

⇒ MP ÷ CP = 114 ÷ 95 = 1.2

⇒ Let CP = 100, then MP = 1.2 × 100 = 120

⇒ New SP = 120 × (100 − 11) ÷ 100

⇒ New SP = 120 × 89 ÷ 100 = 1.2 × 89 = 106.8

⇒ New Profit = SP − CP = 106.8 − 100 = 6.8

⇒ Profit% = (6.8 ÷ 100) × 100 = 6.8%

**∴ The correct answer is 6.8 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Cost Price Relation

The ratio between Marked Price (MP) and Cost Price (CP) is given by MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%). If there is a loss, Profit% is replaced by −Loss%.

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the equivalent single discount is (d₁ + d₂ − d₁d₂ ÷ 100)%.

Net Profit with Discount

Net Profit % = [Markup% − Discount% − (Markup% × Discount%) ÷ 100], where Markup is calculated over CP.</p
